# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

# Dailies Core Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** From a repository URL, produce a fact-checked, narrated MP4 reel of its recorded coding-agent sessions through a resumable pipeline and a CLI.

**Architecture:** A pnpm TypeScript monorepo. `packages/core` holds every shared schema; each other package exposes plain functions over those schemas. A durable runner executes stages in order and persists each stage's artifact so a run can resume.

**Tech Stack:** Node 22+, pnpm workspaces, TypeScript (strict, ESM), zod, vitest, OpenAI SDK against an OpenAI-compatible gateway, neatlogs SDK, Remotion 4, better-sqlite3, ffmpeg, git, Entire CLI.

**Spec:** `docs/specs/2026-10-11-dailies-design.md`

This plan covers Tier 1 of the spec. The web app, evaluation harness, runtime read-back and deployment are separate plans that build on the interfaces fixed here.

## Global Constraints

- Node `>=22`. TypeScript `strict: true`, `"type": "module"`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.
- Internal packages are consumed as TypeScript source: `"exports": { ".": "./src/index.ts" }`. No build step; run with `tsx`, check with `tsc --noEmit`.
- Package names: `@dailies/core`, `@dailies/ingest`, `@dailies/agent`, `@dailies/verify`, `@dailies/voice`, `@dailies/reel`, `@dailies/pipeline`, `@dailies/cli`.
- A package imports another only through its index. Shared types live in `@dailies/core` and nowhere else.
- A task edits files only inside the directories listed under its **Files**. Do not change another package's `package.json`.
- Tests: vitest, files `packages/<name>/test/*.test.ts`. Run one package with `pnpm --filter @dailies/<name> test`.
- No secret ever enters the repository. Configuration comes from `.env` through `loadEnv()`.
- Every model call goes through `@dailies/agent`. No other package imports `openai`.
- Model ids on the gateway: `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-haiku`, `nova-pro`. Gateway base URL: `LITELLM_BASE_URL`. Stay under 50 requests per minute.
- Trace endpoint: `https://ingest.neatlogs.com`.
- A verdict is `verified` only on positive evidence. Anything unknown is `unverifiable`, never `verified` and never `contradicted`.
- Commit after every green test cycle with a short imperative message.
- Once code exists, locate it with `entire graph search` before broad grep, as `CLAUDE.md` instructs.

## Review Focus

1. A repository with no checkpoints, or none inside the window: the run ends early with a clear message and no render. Pinned in Task 2 and Task 10.
2. A tool result of several megabytes or with ANSI colour codes: entries are truncated head-and-tail, colour codes are stripped, memory stays flat. Pinned in Task 2 and Task 4.
3. A claim quote that differs from the transcript only by whitespace or Markdown marks: still matched. A quote that is not in the entry: dropped. Pinned in Task 4.
4. A test run whose output the parser does not recognise: `unknown`, so the claim is `unverifiable`. Pinned in Task 4.
5. Narration audio whose pause count does not equal the line count: timings fall back to proportional alignment and never throw. Pinned in Task 5.
6. A model reply that is not valid JSON for the schema: one repair turn, then the stage fails and the runner retries it. Pinned in Task 3.
7. A secret inside a human prompt or a tool result: redacted at ingest, before any model or renderer sees it. Pinned in Task 1 and Task 2.

## File Structure

```
package.json  pnpm-workspace.yaml  tsconfig.base.json  vitest.config.ts  .nvmrc
packages/core/src/      schema.ts ids.ts redact.ts env.ts budget.ts facts.ts index.ts
packages/ingest/src/    git.ts checkpoints.ts transcript.ts trailers.ts window.ts index.ts
packages/agent/src/     router.ts meter.ts limiter.ts loop.ts tools.ts trace.ts mock.ts index.ts
packages/verify/src/    commands.ts results.ts rules.ts quote.ts ground.ts style.ts index.ts
packages/voice/src/     gemini.ts wav.ts silence.ts align.ts index.ts
packages/reel/src/      timeline.ts srt.ts theme.ts render.ts index.ts
packages/reel/src/remotion/   index.ts Root.tsx Reel.tsx scenes/*.tsx
packages/pipeline/src/  db.ts store.ts runner.ts types.ts index.ts
packages/pipeline/src/stages/   ingest.ts edit.ts verify.ts script.ts ground.ts voice.ts render.ts review.ts gate.ts
packages/pipeline/src/prompts/  editor.ts extractor.ts judge.ts writer.ts entail.ts reviewer.ts
packages/cli/src/       index.ts run.ts verify.ts
packages/cli/bin/       dailies entire-dailies
```

## Task order

960	### Task 2b: Ingest performance
961	
962	Measured on real repositories after Task 2: ingesting 12 sessions of a public repository with 89 checkpoints took 248 seconds; a one-session ingest of another took 79 seconds. Both are dominated by one network round trip per lazily fetched blob and one `git` process per file read. The target is an ingest a person will wait for.
963	
964	**Files:** `packages/ingest/src/**`, `packages/ingest/test/**`
965	
966	**Interfaces:**
967	- Consumes and produces: unchanged. Every exported name and signature of `@dailies/ingest` stays as it is. One addition: `ingest` accepts an optional `onProgress?: (message: string) => void`.
968	
969	Required changes:
970	
971	- **Clone filter.** Clone with `--filter=blob:limit=3m` instead of `blob:none`. Ordinary source blobs and compact transcripts then arrive in the first pack; only the multi-megabyte `full.jsonl` files stay remote, and they are never read.
972	- **Batched object reads.** Read checkpoint files through one long-lived `git cat-file --batch` process per ingest (write object names, read sized replies) instead of one `git show` per file. A blob that is missing locally and larger than the filter is fetched once with `git fetch origin <oid>`; a failure marks that session as skipped with the reason.
973	- **Read metadata before transcripts.** For every checkpoint read only the small metadata files first, decide which sessions fall inside the window and survive the `maxSessions` cap, and read transcripts only for those.
974	- **Batched diffs.** Produce the patches for all linked commits with one `git log -p --no-walk --format=...` call (NUL-separated, as the trailer parsing already does) instead of one call per commit. Cap at the 60 most recent linked commits; report the number dropped in `skipped`.
975	- **Parsed-session cache.** After parsing and redacting a session, store it as `<dataDir>/cache/sessions/<checkpointId>-<n>.json` keyed additionally by the transcript blob's object id. A later ingest reuses it when the object id matches.
976	- **Progress.** Call `onProgress` at each phase with a short message (`cloning`, `read 89 checkpoints`, `12 sessions in window`, `parsing 4/12`, `diffs for 60 commits`).
977

980	| Case | Target |
981	|---|---|
982	| Cold ingest of `https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun`, 12 sessions | under 60 s |
983	| The same again, repository and cache present | under 8 s |
984	| All existing ingest tests | still pass unchanged |

987	- [ ] **Step 2: Run.** Expected: FAIL.

989	- [ ] **Step 4: Run all ingest tests.** Expected: PASS.

## 3. Architecture

One TypeScript monorepo (pnpm workspaces), one Docker image that runs both the web app and the worker, one SQLite database and one data directory on a volume.

```
apps/web           Next.js: landing, app UI, API routes, SSE progress stream
packages/core      shared types and zod schemas, ids, config, budget, redaction
packages/ingest    git + Entire checkpoint reader -> normalized sessions
packages/agent     model router, agent loop, tools, tracing and steering wiring
packages/verify    claim extraction, verifiers, grounding gate
packages/voice     text-to-speech and timing
packages/reel      Remotion scenes, composition, render API
packages/pipeline  stages and the durable runner
packages/cli       `dailies` binary and the `entire-dailies` plugin shim
packages/capture   Playwright live-UI capture            (tier 3)
packages/mcp       MCP server                            (tier 3)
eval/              benchmarks, pinned datasets, results
business/          business plan export, budget generator, actuals
.neatroots/checks/ run checks as YAML
```

Package boundaries are chosen so that each can be built and tested on its own: every package exposes plain functions over the schemas in `packages/core` and none reaches into another's internals.

### Run lifecycle

A **run** turns (repo, time window) into a reel. It is a fixed sequence of stages. Each stage reads the artifacts of earlier stages, writes one JSON artifact (plus files) and is idempotent.

```
ingest -> edit -> verify -> script -> ground -> voice -> footage -> render -> review -> gate -> publish
                                ^                                              |
                                +---------- re-cut (at most 2 loops) ----------+
```

The runner records every stage attempt in SQLite (status, attempt number, timings, artifact path, error). On process start it resumes unfinished runs from their last completed stage. Each stage has its own retry policy with backoff. `review` may send the run back to `script`, `voice` or `render`. `gate` ends in `needs_approval`, `blocked` (with reasons) or `approved`; `publish` only runs from `approved`.

### Data model

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `repos` | URL, default branch, last checkpoint covered, stored preferences |
| `runs` | repo, window, status, cost so far, budget, trace id |
| `stages` | run, name, status, attempt, timings, artifact path, error |
| `claims` | run, session, quote, kind, verdict, evidence refs |
| `lines` | run, scene, narration text, evidence refs, audio path, duration |
| `reels` | run, video path, subtitles, poster, status (draft / approved / published) |
| `feedback` | repo, reel, free text, resulting preference |
| `events` | run, timestamp, stage, message (drives the live progress stream) |

Artifacts (cloned repos, stage JSON, audio, frames, MP4) live under one data directory behind a small storage interface.

165	## 7. Surfaces
166	
167	| Route | Purpose |
168	|---|---|
169	| `/` | Landing: one claim, one call to action, a real reel playing |
170	| `/new` | Paste a repository URL, choose a window |
171	| `/r/[run]` | Live run: stages, events, cost so far |
172	| `/reel/[id]` | Player, evidence panel (each line and its sources), flags, cost, trace reference |
173	| `/inbox` | Reels waiting for approval or feedback |
174	| `/gallery` | Published reels |
175	| `/economics` | Plan versus actual cost per reel |
176	| `/health` | Evaluation scorecard, detections, open fixes for the agent itself |
177	
178	Viewing is public. Starting a run is rate-limited per address and capped per day because every run costs money. Approving requires the owner token.
179	
180	CLI: `dailies run <repo|path> [--since 24h] [--no-render] [--out dir]`, `dailies verify <repo|path>`.
181	
182	## 8. Failure handling
183	
184	| Failure | Response |
185	|---|---|
186	| Repo has no checkpoints | Run ends early with a clear message; nothing is rendered |
187	| Model rate limit or server error | Backoff, then the fallback provider |
188	| Budget reached mid-run | Run stops in `blocked`, partial artifacts kept |
189	| Text-to-speech fails | Retry, alternate voice, then captions-only cut labelled as such |
190	| Render crashes | Retry the stage from its inputs; storyboard and audio are reused |
191	| Review still failing after two loops | Run ends in `blocked` with the findings attached |
192	| Process restart | Unfinished runs resume from the last completed stage |
193	| Entire CLI enrichment unavailable | Marked `skipped`; the run continues on git data |
194	
195	## 9. Evaluation
196	
197	- **Mutation benchmark.** For every verified `tests_pass` or `build_passes` claim, flip the recorded tool result to a failure; the verdict must become contradicted. For every contradicted one, flip it to a pass; the verdict must become verified. This shows a green verdict is never vacuous.
198	- **Grounding benchmark.** Inject fabricated narration lines (wrong numbers, features absent from the diff) next to true ones. The gate must reject all fabricated lines and keep the true ones.
199	- **Field sample.** Run the verifier over sessions from public repositories pinned by commit. Hand-label a sample of flagged claims; the labels' hash is committed before the run. Report precision. Results are aggregate; no repository is named.
200	- **Baseline comparison.** The same sessions through a single-prompt summariser with no gates versus the full pipeline: unsupported statements per reel, tokens and cost.
201	
202	Scorecards are committed as JSON and Markdown, failures included.
203	
204	## 10. Testing
205	
206	Unit tests for the parsers (checkpoint reader, test-runner output, trailer mapping), verifiers, grounding gate, redaction, budget and the runner's resume logic, written test-first. Fixture checkpoints are small synthetic trees built in the tests. One end-to-end test runs the pipeline with a mock model and a stub renderer.
207	
208	## 11. Privacy and safety
209	
210	Only public repositories. Redaction runs at ingest and again at the gate, and the gate fails closed. Reels about a repository are unlisted until its owner approves. Evaluation statistics about other people's repositories are published only in aggregate.
211	
212	## 12. Known limits
213	
214	- Verification rests on what the session recorded. A command the agent ran outside the recorded session is invisible.
215	- `implemented` claims rely on a model's judgement, constrained by a quoted, validated hunk.
216	- The voice is synthetic.

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/` | Landing: one claim, one call to action, a real reel playing |
| `/new` | Paste a repository URL, choose a window |
| `/r/[run]` | Live run: stages, events, cost so far |
| `/reel/[id]` | Player, evidence panel (each line and its sources), flags, cost, trace reference |
| `/inbox` | Reels waiting for approval or feedback |
| `/gallery` | Published reels |
| `/economics` | Plan versus actual cost per reel |
| `/health` | Evaluation scorecard, detections, open fixes for the agent itself |

Viewing is public. Starting a run is rate-limited per address and capped per day because every run costs money. Approving requires the owner token.

CLI: `dailies run <repo|path> [--since 24h] [--no-render] [--out dir]`, `dailies verify <repo|path>`.

## 8. Failure handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| Repo has no checkpoints | Run ends early with a clear message; nothing is rendered |
| Model rate limit or server error | Backoff, then the fallback provider |
| Budget reached mid-run | Run stops in `blocked`, partial artifacts kept |
| Text-to-speech fails | Retry, alternate voice, then captions-only cut labelled as such |
| Render crashes | Retry the stage from its inputs; storyboard and audio are reused |
| Review still failing after two loops | Run ends in `blocked` with the findings attached |
| Process restart | Unfinished runs resume from the last completed stage |
| Entire CLI enrichment unavailable | Marked `skipped`; the run continues on git data |

## 9. Evaluation

- **Mutation benchmark.** For every verified `tests_pass` or `build_passes` claim, flip the recorded tool result to a failure; the verdict must become contradicted. For every contradicted one, flip it to a pass; the verdict must become verified. This shows a green verdict is never vacuous.
- **Grounding benchmark.** Inject fabricated narration lines (wrong numbers, features absent from the diff) next to true ones. The gate must reject all fabricated lines and keep the true ones.
- **Field sample.** Run the verifier over sessions from public repositories pinned by commit. Hand-label a sample of flagged claims; the labels' hash is committed before the run. Report precision. Results are aggregate; no repository is named.
- **Baseline comparison.** The same sessions through a single-prompt summariser with no gates versus the full pipeline: unsupported statements per reel, tokens and cost.

Scorecards are committed as JSON and Markdown, failures included.

## 10. Testing

Unit tests for the parsers (checkpoint reader, test-runner output, trailer mapping), verifiers, grounding gate, redaction, budget and the runner's resume logic, written test-first. Fixture checkpoints are small synthetic trees built in the tests. One end-to-end test runs the pipeline with a mock model and a stub renderer.

## 11. Privacy and safety

Only public repositories. Redaction runs at ingest and again at the gate, and the gate fails closed. Reels about a repository are unlisted until its owner approves. Evaluation statistics about other people's repositories are published only in aggregate.

## 12. Known limits

- Verification rests on what the session recorded. A command the agent ran outside the recorded session is invisible.
- `implemented` claims rely on a model's judgement, constrained by a quoted, validated hunk.
- The voice is synthetic.

456:- `cloneOrUpdate`: a local path is used in place. A URL is cloned with `git clone --filter=blob:none` into `<dataDir>/repos/<owner>__<name>`, or fetched if present. Then `git fetch origin '+refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'` and `git fetch origin '+refs/heads/entire/*:refs/remotes/origin/entire/*'`; a failure of either fetch is tolerated.
494:- [ ] **Step 6: Run against a real repository** and record the output in the commit message body: `pnpm tsx -e "import('@dailies/ingest').then(async m => { const a = await m.ingest({ repoUrl: 'https://github.com/entireio/cli', dataDir: '.dailies', since: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z', until: new Date().toISOString(), maxSessions: 3 }); console.log(a.sessions.map(s => [s.id, s.entries.length, s.commits.length])); })"`. Expected: three sessions with non-zero entry counts.
665:export async function voiceLines(lines: { id: string; text: string }[], o: { provider: TtsProvider; voice: string; outDir: string; maxCalls: number }): Promise<{ mode: 'voiced' | 'captions'; audioPath: string | null; timings: LineTiming[]; calls: number }>
676:- **`voiceLines`.** Uses a cached WAV under `outDir/cache/<sha256 of provider name, voice and text>.wav` when present (zero calls) — the `TtsProvider` interface exposes only `name`, not a model list, so the cache key is keyed on that. Otherwise synthesises, writes `outDir/narration.wav`, detects silences and aligns. On `TtsQuotaError`, or when `maxCalls` is zero, it returns `mode: 'captions'`, `audioPath: null` and `estimateTimings`.
712:export async function renderReel(i: { storyboard: Storyboard; timings: LineTiming[]; audioPath: string | null; outDir: string }): Promise<RenderArtifact>
713:export async function renderStills(i: { storyboard: Storyboard; timings: LineTiming[]; outDir: string }): Promise<{ sceneId: string; path: string }[]>
720:- **Rendering.** `bundle({ entryPoint: <src/remotion/index.ts>, publicDir: <outDir>/public })` with the narration copied to `public/narration.wav`; `selectComposition({ id: 'Reel', inputProps })`; `renderMedia({ codec: 'h264', outputLocation: <outDir>/reel.mp4 })`. The poster is `renderStill` at the middle of the title scene. `renderReel` writes `reel.mp4`, `reel.srt` and `poster.png` into `outDir` and returns absolute paths. `renderStills` writes one PNG per scene at that scene's middle frame, named `NN-<type>.png` in scene order; the review stage uses them. Its signature carries no audio flag, so stills are always drawn as the captions cut: that is the tighter layout and shows every piece of text a frame can carry.

62	### Run lifecycle
63	
64	A **run** turns (repo, time window) into a reel. It is a fixed sequence of stages. Each stage reads the artifacts of earlier stages, writes one JSON artifact (plus files) and is idempotent.
65	
66	```
67	ingest -> edit -> verify -> script -> ground -> voice -> footage -> render -> review -> gate -> publish
68	                                ^                                              |
69	                                +---------- re-cut (at most 2 loops) ----------+
70	```
71	
72	The runner records every stage attempt in SQLite (status, attempt number, timings, artifact path, error). On process start it resumes unfinished runs from their last completed stage. Each stage has its own retry policy with backoff. `review` may send the run back to `script`, `voice` or `render`. `gate` ends in `needs_approval`, `blocked` (with reasons) or `approved`; `publish` only runs from `approved`.

file.content:
### Run lifecycle

A **run** turns (repo, time window) into a reel. It is a fixed sequence of stages. Each stage reads the artifacts of earlier stages, writes one JSON artifact (plus files) and is idempotent.

```
ingest -> edit -> verify -> script -> ground -> voice -> footage -> render -> review -> gate -> publish
                                ^                                              |

# Dailies

Dailies turns the recorded coding-agent sessions of a repository into a short narrated video reel: what an AI agent did, how it validated the work, and where its own account of events does not match the record.

Point it at a public repository and a time window. It reads the Entire checkpoints for that window, picks out the claims the agent made about its own work ("tests pass", "the bug is fixed", "I added X"), checks each one against the recorded tool output and the commit diff, and narrates the result as a reel: the problem, the key decisions, the implementation, and the recorded validation. A claim the record contradicts is not hidden — it is shown on screen next to the agent's own words, labelled as a flag. Nothing is said in narration that a line of evidence does not support; a line that fails that check is rewritten or cut before it reaches the screen.

The output of a run is an MP4, an SRT subtitle track, a poster frame, and a gate report of what passed.

## Quick start

```bash
pnpm install
cp .env.example .env   # fill in at least LITELLM_API_KEY

pnpm dailies run https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --since 7d
pnpm dailies verify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --since 7d --json
```

Or, with `packages/cli/bin` on `PATH`:

```bash
dailies run <repo-url|path> [--since 24h|<ISO>] [--max-sessions 12] [--out <dir>] [--no-voice] [--no-review]
dailies verify <repo-url|path> [--since 24h|<ISO>] [--json]
```

`dailies run` clones the repository (or uses a local path as given), builds the reel, and prints each stage's progress as it happens, then the final status, the cost of the run, and the paths of the MP4, subtitles and poster. It exits `0` when the reel is ready for approval, `2` when the run ends early with nothing to render (for example, no agent sessions in the window), and `1` on failure.

`dailies verify` runs only ingestion and claim verification and prints a table — verdict, kind, session, a short quote, and why — without rendering anything. Pass `--json` for the raw claims.

With `packages/cli/bin` on `PATH`, the Entire CLI can also run it as a plugin: `entire dailies run .`.

## Environment

Configuration comes from a `.env` file at the repository root (see `.env.example`); no secret is ever committed. A run needs at least `LITELLM_API_KEY` — without it, both commands exit with a clear message instead of failing partway through.

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | Enables tracing for the run. Without it, tracing is a no-op. |
| `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` | Trace ingest endpoint. Defaults to `https://ingest.neatlogs.com`. |
| `LITELLM_API_KEY` | Key for the model gateway every model call goes through. Required. |
| `LITELLM_BASE_URL` | Gateway base URL. |
| `VENICE_API_KEY` | Fallback model provider, used when the primary gateway is unavailable. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEYS` | Comma-separated keys for narration text-to-speech. Without one, or with `--no-voice`, the reel still renders — as a captions-only cut. |

`DAILIES_DATA_DIR` (not in `.env.example`, but read the same way) sets where clones, the run database and rendered artifacts live; it defaults to `.dailies` under the current directory.

## How a run proceeds

```
ingest -> edit -> verify -> script -> ground -> voice -> render -> gate
                      ^                                     |
                      +-------- re-cut (at most 2 loops) ----+
```

Each stage reads the artifacts of the ones before it and writes its own; a crash resumes from the last completed stage rather than starting over. `gate` checks grounding, secrets, cost and (when not disabled) review, and ends the run `needs_approval` or `blocked` with reasons.

## Limits

- Verification rests on what the session recorded. A command the agent ran outside the recorded session is invisible.
- `implemented` claims rely on a model's judgement, constrained by a quoted, validated hunk.
- The voice is synthetic.
- Session formats other than Claude Code's are parsed best-effort.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 10 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 600000ms are capped to 600000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

- Produces: the commands below.

```
dailies run <repo-url|path> [--since 24h|<ISO>] [--max-sessions 12] [--out <dir>] [--no-voice] [--no-review]
dailies verify <repo-url|path> [--since 24h|<ISO>] [--json]
```

- `run` creates a run, executes the pipeline, prints each event as it happens, then prints the final status, reason, cost, and the paths of the MP4, subtitles and poster. Exit code 0 for `needs_approval`, 2 for `blocked`, 1 for `failed`. The whole command runs under `initTracing(env, 'dailies-reel')` with the run id attached, and calls `shutdownTracing()` in `finally`.
- `verify` runs ingest and the verify stage only and prints a table: verdict, kind, session, quote cut to 80 characters, reason. `--json` prints the claims array.
- `--since 24h` accepts `<n>h` and `<n>d`; anything else is parsed as an ISO date.
- Open from Task 8: `--max-sessions` has no way into the ingest stage. `buildStages(deps)` takes `StageDeps`, which holds no session cap, and the run record holds none either, so the stage calls `ingest()` with its default of 12. An optional `maxSessions` on `StageDeps`, passed through by the ingest stage, would close it.
- `bin/dailies` and `bin/entire-dailies` are identical shell shims that run `tsx <repo>/packages/cli/src/index.ts "$@"`. With `packages/cli/bin` on `PATH`, `entire dailies run .` works because the Entire CLI dispatches `entire <name>` to an executable named `entire-<name>`.

### Task 10: CLI and end-to-end

Depends on Tasks 8 and 9.

**Files:** `packages/cli/src/{index.ts,run.ts,verify.ts}`, `packages/cli/bin/{dailies,entire-dailies}`, `packages/cli/test/e2e.test.ts`, `README.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `buildStages`, `openDb`, `createRun`, `runPipeline`, `getRun`, `listEvents`; `createRouter`, `CostMeter`, `initTracing`, `shutdownTracing`, `traced`; `createGeminiTts`; `loadEnv`, `DEFAULT_BUDGET`.
- Produces: the commands below.
- Corrected from the plan as written: `@dailies/pipeline`'s index exports `buildStages`/`recordSpend` and only the stage *artifact types*, not `ingestStage`, `verifyStage` or `reviewStage` themselves — the plan's `reviewStage`, bare `ingest` and `completeJson` are not reachable through that one door and are not used. `run` inserts no review stage (see the note below); `verify` reuses `buildStages(deps)` filtered to `ingest` and `verify` rather than calling `ingest()`/`completeJson()` directly, so claim extraction has exactly one implementation.
- `reviewStage` is not exported from `@dailies/pipeline` (only its artifact type is) — an omission in Task 9's work, outside the files Task 10 may touch to fix. `--no-review` is accepted on the command line for the documented surface below, but there is currently nothing for it to disable: every run executes `buildStages`' eight stages unmodified.

```
dailies run <repo-url|path> [--since 24h|<ISO>] [--max-sessions 12] [--out <dir>] [--no-voice] [--no-review]
dailies verify <repo-url|path> [--since 24h|<ISO>] [--json]
```

- `run` creates a run, executes the pipeline, prints each event as it happens, then prints the final status, reason, cost, and the paths of the MP4, subtitles and poster. Exit code 0 for `needs_approval`, 2 for `blocked`, 1 for `failed`. The whole command runs under `initTracing(env, 'dailies-reel')` with the run id attached, and calls `shutdownTracing()` in `finally`.
- `verify` runs ingest and the verify stage only and prints a table: verdict, kind, session, quote cut to 80 characters, reason. `--json` prints the claims array.
- `--since 24h` accepts `<n>h` and `<n>d`; anything else is parsed as an ISO date.
- Open from Task 8: `--max-sessions` has no way into the ingest stage. `buildStages(deps)` takes `StageDeps`, which holds no session cap, and the run record holds none either, so the stage calls `ingest()` with its default of 12. An optional `maxSessions` on `StageDeps`, passed through by the ingest stage, would close it.

content.content:
## 01:14 | task/8-stages
Task 8 (Pipeline stages) complete on branch task/8-stages, 20 commits, not pushed, not merged. 8 stages (ingest, edit, verify, script, ground, voice, render, gate) + stages/index.ts (buildStages, recordSpend) + 5 prompt files; 118 new tests in packages/pipeline/test/stages (10 files), repo-wide 301 passed / 1 skipped (agent live test, no key), typecheck clean. Plan file fixed for Task 8 and Task 10 (commit 6e58729).

Deviations Task 10 must know: StageDeps has `db` (addCost needs it); `recordSpend(deps, reviewStage(deps))` must wrap the review stage or its spend is not recorded; `--max-sessions` has no path into the ingest stage (optional `maxSessions` on StageDeps would close it); @dailies/pipeline now depends on zod and its index re-exports ./stages/index.

Open, outside Task 8's files: @dailies/ingest `repoDirName` puts URL userinfo into the clone directory name and keys the clone on owner/name only (two hosts collide); the web entry point must restrict repoUrl (the stage passes run.repoUrl through because the CLI needs local paths).

## 01:28 | task/14-web-ui
Task 14 (Web interface) complete on branch task/14-web-ui, 7 commits on top of e042735, not pushed, not merged. Four pages (/, /r/[id], /reel/[id], /gallery) in the Loupe direction, all data through the HTTP API; 111 new tests in apps/web/test/ui (web suite 145 passed, root suite 199 passed / 1 skipped), typecheck clean, `pnpm --filter @dailies/web build` clean. Seed for looking at the pages: `pnpm --filter @dailies/web exec tsx test/ui/seed.ts <dataDir>`.

Open, outside Task 14's files (all in apps/web/src/app/api/reels/[id]/route.ts): it returns the `script` artifact as `storyboard`, which is the pre-grounding `{ storyboard, discarded }`, where the final one is `ground.json`.storyboard; it reads `voice.voiceMode` but the stage writes `mode`, so voiceMode is always null; there is no endpoint for transcript entries or patches, so a source opens only to what the storyboard and the claims quote. The reel page works around the first (unwraps the artifact, takes each line's final wording from reel.srt) but the evidence of a rewritten line stays the pre-rewrite one until the route reads `ground`.

## 01:41 | task/16-loupe-reel
Task 16 (Reel scenes in the Loupe direction) complete on branch task/16-loupe-reel, 5 commits on top of bf8a8a3, not pushed, not merged. One continuous film strip + a persistent loupe (lens.ts: shots, lensPath, framing), pencil marks (pencil.ts, marks.tsx), seven scenes as { Film, Glass, Over }, measured text fitting; docs/design.md is the design reference. Reel suite 181 passed (9 files), root typecheck clean; fixture reel renders in ~40-70 s on this (shared, loaded) machine.

What merging branches must know: core Scene end now has `unverified: z.number().int().default(0)`, so the inferred type requires it wherever an end scene is built as a typed literal (zod-parsed input is unaffected). renderStills passes an internal `settled: true` prop, so review stills show every pencil mark and the terminal's last step, which in the reel wait for their narration line. Martian Mono comes without its width axis from @remotion/google-fonts, so code is set at normal width, 30-32 px. theme.test.ts no longer pins backdrop luma (the Loupe room is darker than blackdetect's threshold by design); the lit glass is pinned instead (theme.test.ts + lens.test.ts) and render.test.ts still runs blackdetect on the whole reel.

Strengthen userinfo stripping and terminal sanitization

for a password that itself contains an "@". sanitizeForTerminal widens
its match from the C0/C1 control range to every Unicode format and
separator character (covers bidi overrides and zero-width characters,
not just ASCII escape sequences) and escapes a literal backslash too,
so the encoding stays unambiguous.

EOF
)"
